Secrets of Old Rio — 4 hours — USD 215 per person
Private tour, minimum 2 people, with an English-speaking guide.
Discover the history of old Rio de Janeiro, its colonial past, traditions and religious monuments. Your guide meets you at your hotel and takes you to the historic centre, where you learn how the city, founded in 1565, got its name. See Candelária Church, built in 1775, and São Bento Monastery, with its Baroque architecture and art. Visit the Lapa Arches, built in 1732 as part of the water supply system carrying water from the Carioca River to the city centre.
Continue to the Municipal Theatre, modelled on European theatres and reminiscent of the Paris Opera.
At Praça XV, see the Imperial Palace, from whose balcony the abolition of slavery in Brazil was announced, Tiradentes Palace, the cathedral built in 1808 as a royal church, and the 16th-century Carmelite convent.
Largo do Boticário has mosaic-fronted buildings, historic architecture and century-old trees. Visit Rio's Metropolitan Cathedral, which can hold up to 20,000 people.
The walk ends at the historic Confeitaria Colombo, a symbol of Rio and a meeting place for the city's elite since the late 19th century. You can try its pastries and desserts.
Food and drinks at Confeitaria Colombo are not included.

Helicopter flight — price on request
The price depends on the flight duration.
See Rio de Janeiro from the air: the blue ocean, forested mountains, white-sand beaches, yachts and the city panorama.
Flights last from 6 to 13 minutes. Depending on your chosen route, you can see the helipad by Christ the Redeemer, the Botanical Garden, Niemeyer Lake, Leblon, Ipanema, Copacabana and Sugar Loaf.

blocks.text:
Botanical Garden — USD 295 per person
Private tour, minimum 2 people, with an English-speaking guide.
Rio de Janeiro's Botanical Garden was founded in 1808 by the Prince Regent Dom João. Walk along its avenues past sculptures, monuments, small lakes and fountains, with plants from around the world.
The garden has more than 7,000 plant species, including rare and exotic orchids. See the pau-brasil tree, Brazil's national symbol, on Pedro Gordilho Avenue, and the tall imperial palms.
Frei Leandro Lake, named after the garden's first director, is home to giant Victoria water lilies.

Favela tour — USD 130 per person in a group with an English-speaking guide / USD 280 per person privately
Private tour, minimum 2 people, with an English-speaking guide.
Visit Rocinha, Rio de Janeiro's largest favela, to see residents' daily life, the local architecture, narrow streets, busy street trading and small markets selling food and local crafts.
Rio has many favelas, each with its own history and culture. On the jeep tour, you visit Rocinha and other characteristic neighbourhoods before returning to your hotel.

Hang gliding — USD 590 per person
Transfer from your hotel to Pedra Bonita, with views across Rio de Janeiro. Fly over forested mountain slopes and the ocean.
Before the flight, a professional English-speaking instructor gives a detailed safety briefing and explains the rules. After preparation and fitting your equipment, you take a tandem flight with the instructor, landing on Pepino Beach.
Transfers and a video recording of the flight are included.

blocks.text:
**Brazil and Argentina for adults, 2027. Prices for 1–3 travellers.**

The three main stops offer very different experiences. Rio centres on the ocean, mountains and open views. At Iguazu, the city recedes as you explore rainforest, water and long trails through the national parks. Buenos Aires brings you back to city neighbourhoods, squares, the old port, broad avenues, cafés and evening tango.

The itinerary combines journeys, transfers with a driver and domestic flights from Rio to Iguazu and Buenos Aires. Programme tours in Rio, Iguazu and Buenos Aires have English-speaking guides. Optional excursions have their own conditions.

Your first 3 nights are in Rio, allowing time for the city's 2 main viewpoints and optional activities. Iguazu takes 2 nights, with a separate route on each side of the border: Brazil offers a view of the full line of cascades, while Argentina's walkways bring you closer to the river. After the city tour in Buenos Aires, a free day lets you explore the city or visit the delta, a ranch or Uruguay.

The sequence also spreads out the activity. Your arrival day is free after the international flight. Two full days in Rio are followed by a short flight and time in nature at Iguazu. After your second day at the falls, you fly straight to Buenos Aires, where the pace becomes calmer and more urban.

## Optional excursions in Iguazu and Buenos Aires

### Rafain show — USD 185 per person

Drinks are not included.

Spend an evening at Rafain, an air-conditioned restaurant seating around 1,200 guests, with parking.

Choose from fresh beef and pork dishes and a buffet of vegetables, fruit and desserts.

Dinner accompanies a show by Latin American performers, with traditional music, folk dances and contemporary choreography.

### Macuco Safari — USD 135 per person

An addition to the Brazilian Falls tour.

Travel by jeep through tropical rainforest with a guide who introduces the national park's nature.

Continue on foot to a purpose-built platform on the Iguazu River, then board a boat to approach the falls.

You come close to the powerful water, surrounded by green slopes and tropical plants, with spray, the roar of the falls and panoramic views.

For guests at Belmond Hotel das Cataratas, price on request.

### Bird Park — USD 60 per person

An addition to the Brazilian Falls tour.

The Bird Park is beside Iguazu National Park, with exotic birds living among tropical forest.

Walk through large aviaries where colourful birds fly and move freely among the vegetation.

For guests at Belmond Hotel das Cataratas, price on request.

### Helicopter flight over the falls — USD 255 per person

An addition to the Brazilian Falls tour. Minimum 4 people.

See the scale and power of Iguazu Falls from the air.

The 10-minute flight offers a panorama of the entire waterfall complex surrounded by dense tropical forest.

### Tigre and the northern suburbs of Buenos Aires — USD 100 per person in a group with an English-speaking guide, USD 350 per person privately (shared boat)

Private tour, minimum 2 people, with an English-speaking guide.

Visit Tigre, a town on the water about 40 km from central Buenos Aires, often called a “little Venice” for its rivers and canals.

It is a popular place for Argentines to relax in nature.

On the way, explore the northern districts of Buenos Aires Province and visit San Isidro, an elegant, scenic suburb with a different feel from the busy city centre.

Continue to Tigre to walk around its historic centre and take a boat trip through the rivers and canals of the delta.

### Montevideo, Uruguay — full-day tour — USD 800 per person

Private tour, minimum 2 people, with an English-speaking guide on the city tour.

Travel from Buenos Aires to Uruguay, across the Río de la Plata. The country is known for colonial towns, beaches and its cultural heritage. Early in the morning, transfer to Buenos Aires port and cross by ferry. On arrival, a guide meets you for a tour by car of Montevideo's main sights.

Visit Montevideo port, Independence Square, the city centre, the Old Town and the Cathedral.

After the tour, you have free time to explore before your return ferry.

Return to Buenos Aires by the same route, with a transfer from the port to your hotel.

Ferry tickets are included.

### Fiesta Gaucho — full-day tour — USD 320 per person in a group with an English-speaking guide, USD 490 per person privately

Group tour with an English-speaking guide.

Discover rural Argentina and the traditions, daily life and folklore of the gauchos, the country's horsemen and cattle herders.

The excursion takes place at a traditional estancia about 80 km from Buenos Aires.

Once nomadic, many gauchos later settled on ranches to farm and raise cattle. Today they preserve ancestral traditions and demonstrate their riding skills.

See traditional gaucho skills, including horsemanship, handling a lasso and the boleadoras, and learn about Argentine cattle-ranching traditions.

Duration: 8 hours.

A traditional Argentine lunch is included.
